board.key.what: type at the board's own keyboard, a character at a time, which is what the hardware sends: it holds the last key pressed and the firmware polls it

params.name: node
params.what: which board; refused when absent, when the node is not running, or when its backend has no keyboard

params.name: text
params.what: the characters to send, each one a keypress; refused when absent or empty

board.key.answers: `typed` is how many characters were sent, not how many the firmware read: it polls, so typing faster than it polls loses keys.

example.what: type a word at the board's keyboard

board.press.what: hold one of a board's own buttons down, or let it go, so a long press reaches the firmware as a long press rather than as a tap

params.name: node
params.what: which board; refused when absent, when the node is not running, or when its backend has no buttons

params.name: pin
params.what: the GPIO the button sits on, as the board profile declares it; refused when absent or not a number

params.name: down
params.what: true holds it, false releases it; absent counts as a release

board.press.answers: The answer repeats what was asked, which is the acknowledgement that the press reached the board at all. Whether the firmware did anything with it is board.screen's question.

board.screen.what: measure what a board's own display is showing as numbers rather than as a picture, so a script can tell whether a press or a keystroke changed anything

params.name: node
params.what: which board; refused when absent, when the node is not running, or when its backend has no display

board.screen.answers: A board whose backend models a display but has drawn nothing yet answers with `has_screen` false and nothing else, which is a fact about the board rather than a failure. Otherwise `lit` counts the non-zero bytes of the framebuffer, for how much is on, and `digest` is a hex hash of the whole frame, for whether it is the same frame - which is what a wait for the screen to change compares.

example.what: check whether the display has changed

board.touch.what: put a finger on the board's panel at a point, or take it off, in the panel's own pixels rather than the drawn screen's

params.name: node
params.what: which board; refused when absent, when the node is not running, or when its backend has no touch panel

params.name: x
params.what: the column, from the panel's own left edge; refused when absent or not a number

params.name: y
params.what: the row, from the panel's own top edge; refused when absent or not a number

params.name: down
params.what: true touches, false lifts off; absent counts as a lift off

example.what: touch the middle of the panel
